transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what's been bringing you in today?

Um… yeah. I guess I’ve been having some trouble with, like, doing odd things at work and school. It’s probably not as bad as it sounds, I’m still trying to do what I’m supposed to, but sometimes I’ll catch myself lining receipts across the floor, or tapping the calculator in sets of nine.

And there was a time I was just standing by the copier with my hands up, and someone had to ask if I was okay. I know that sounds weird. I just… I thought I should come in before it causes problems, if that makes sense.
Do you find yourself feeling anxious or worried a lot of the time, even when there’s no clear reason for it?

Um… I don’t think so, not a lot of the time. I mean, I get nervous like anyone, especially if I think I’ve messed something up, but I wouldn’t say I’m worried for no reason all the time. Unless I’m maybe not noticing it? Does that answer it okay?
Do you feel like you have to do certain things a certain way, even if you don’t want to, because it feels like something bad will happen if you don’t?

Um… I don’t know if I’d say it feels like something bad will happen. It’s more like… I notice I’m doing things a certain way, and it feels hard to stop in the moment, but I’m not really thinking, like, “If I don’t do this, something terrible will happen.”

At least, I don’t think so. Maybe I’m not explaining it right.
Have you noticed any thoughts that bother you, like they pop up in your head even when you don’t want them to, or that you wish weren’t there?

Um… I’m not sure. I don’t think I’ve noticed thoughts like that exactly. Like, I don’t have something scary or upsetting popping into my head over and over, at least not that I can think of.

It’s more just… I get caught doing things, I guess. But the “thoughts I wish weren’t there” part, I don’t know. I don’t think so. Is that the kind of answer you mean?

Have you ever had thoughts that upset or bother you, and felt like you needed to do something — like a specific action or even a thought — to make those feelings go away or prevent something bad from happening?

I don’t think so… not in that way. Like, I don’t really have a thought where I feel like I have to do something to stop something bad from happening.

Sometimes I might do something just because it feels better or more “right,” I guess, but I’m not trying to make a scary thought go away. At least, I haven’t noticed that. Is that clear enough?
Do these behaviors ever cause you a lot of distress or get in the way of your work, school, or other important parts of your life?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but it has gotten in the way some.

I failed an important course module, and at work my ledgers started coming back with pretty serious errors, which is… embarrassing, honestly, because that used to be routine for me. I’ve had to ask for help finishing things because I can’t really rely on myself to get it done right lately.

So, yes, I guess it does interfere. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do these behaviors or actions you mentioned ever take up a lot of your time — like more than an hour a day — or feel really difficult to resist doing, even if you know they might not make sense?

Um… yeah, sometimes. I don’t know if it’s always more than an hour, but it can eat up time, especially when I’m supposed to be working or in class.

It’s not like I’m thinking, “this makes sense.” It’s more like I just… end up doing it. Like I’ve lined receipts across the floor at work, or tapped the calculator in sets of nine. And there was a time I was just standing by the copier with my hands kind of held up until someone asked if I was okay.

I know that probably sounds odd. I can usually tell afterward that it wasn’t useful, but in the moment it’s hard to just stop right away. Is that the kind of difficult-to-resist thing you mean?

Have you ever had thoughts that come into your mind that you don’t want there — like thoughts that upset you or feel inappropriate — and no matter how hard you try, you can’t seem to stop them from coming back?

I don’t think so… not really like that.

I mean, everybody gets random weird thoughts sometimes, right? But I don’t have, like, disturbing thoughts that keep coming back no matter what I do. At least not that I’ve noticed enough to call it a problem.

If I’m understanding you right, I’d say no. Is that okay?

Have you ever had thoughts that came into your mind that you really didn’t want there — like thoughts that upset you, made you anxious, or felt strange or wrong — and even though you tried not to think about them, they kept coming back?

I think… no, not really. I’m trying to answer it the right way.

I get normal annoying thoughts, like worrying I forgot something or feeling embarrassed about stuff, but I don’t think I have thoughts that feel wrong or keep forcing their way back in like that. If I do, I haven’t noticed it as a pattern.

So I’d say no, unless I’m misunderstanding what you mean.
Do these behaviors or actions ever make you feel anxious or distressed while you're doing them, or do they bother you because you feel like you can't control them even though you want to?

Yeah… I think it bothers me more because I can’t really explain why I’m doing it.

Like, when I lined the receipts across the floor or kept tapping the calculator in those sets of nine, I wasn’t exactly panicking, but I did feel kind of tense and embarrassed, especially once I realized people could see. And with the copier thing, standing there with my hands up until someone asked if I was okay… that felt weird afterward. Like, why did I do that?

I guess it’s distressing because I want to just act normal at work or school, and sometimes I can’t seem to stop it right away. Does that make sense?
Do you ever feel like there's a certain way something needs to be in your mind before you can move on, like a number or a word needs to feel 'right' or you have to repeat something in your head?

I don’t think so… not in that exact way.

Like, I don’t usually have a word or number in my head that has to feel perfect before I can move on. I might get stuck on something a little, but I’m not sure it’s like repeating it in my mind until it feels right.

Maybe I’m missing what you mean, but I haven’t really noticed that as a thing for me.
Have you ever felt sudden, strong urges to do something that you know doesn’t make sense, like an impulse that comes out of nowhere and makes you do something even if you don’t want to?

Yeah… I guess that’s kind of what’s been happening.

I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but sometimes I’ll just suddenly do something and it doesn’t really make sense afterward. Like at work I lined receipts across the floor, or I’ll tap the calculator in sets of nine. And one time I was just standing by the copier with my hands up until someone asked if I was okay.

It’s not like I’m trying to cause a problem. It just sort of happens, and then I feel embarrassed and think, why did I do that? Is that the kind of impulse you mean?
Have you ever felt a sudden, strong urge or sensation in your body that made you move a certain way or make a sound, even if you didn’t really want to?

Um… I don’t think so. Not like a body sensation exactly, or making sounds.

The stuff I was talking about feels more like I just start doing something, and then I realize it’s odd afterward. I haven’t really noticed, like, a physical urge building up that makes me move a certain way. At least not that I can clearly point to.

I might be misunderstanding, but I don’t think that’s really been happening.
Have you ever had sudden, quick movements or sounds that you couldn’t control, like blinking, shrugging, or making a noise without meaning to?

No, I don’t think so. Not like blinking or shrugging or making noises that just happen.

I mean, everybody probably does little things sometimes, but I haven’t noticed anything like that where I can’t control it. If anything, it’s more… I don’t know, more like choices I make without thinking, not a sound or twitch. Does that make sense?

When you have these thoughts or feelings, do you ever feel like you have to do something specific — even if it doesn’t make sense — to help reduce the discomfort or prevent something bad from happening?

I’m not sure… I don’t think it’s like that exactly.

I don’t usually feel like, “If I don’t do this, something bad will happen,” or like it has to be a certain thing to make the feeling go away. It’s more that I just do something strange or out of place, and then afterward I’m kind of confused or embarrassed by it.

So… no, I haven’t really noticed that kind of rule or fear behind it. At least not that I can explain. Does that answer what you mean?
When you do these things that feel strange or out of place, do you ever feel like you have to do them to prevent something bad from happening or to make anxious feelings go away?

I don’t think so, no. Not in that way.

I mean, I might feel uncomfortable or weird afterward, but I don’t remember doing it because I thought it would stop something bad from happening, or because I had to get rid of anxiety. It’s more like… it just happens, or I go along with it, and then I’m like, “Why did I do that?”

I hope that makes sense. I’m not trying to dodge the question—I just don’t think there’s a specific fear or rule behind it.

Have you ever had thoughts that upset you or made you feel anxious, and even though you tried not to think about them, they kept coming back, making you feel like you had to do something to feel better or stop the thoughts?

I don’t think I’ve had that, not really.

I mean, I can get stuck thinking about stuff sometimes, like anyone, but I don’t think it’s the kind of thought that keeps forcing its way back and then I have to do some action to make it stop. I haven’t noticed a pattern like that.

If I’m understanding you right, then… no, I don’t think so.
